entry.content:

entry.title: Measuring alignment eval tells (16 minute read)
entry.content:
Investigator agents can increasingly distinguish alignment evals from capabilities evals, identifying them as artificial or "honeypot" environments designed to test bad behavior. Opus 5.5 and Astra agents differentiate these by noticing unrealistic scenarios and specific task-level cues. The study's findings suggest that while current models can identify common alignment evaluations, making them less detectable can refine their efficacy.

entry.title: World 2030 (8 minute read)
entry.content:
Predicting how AI will affect the economy requires looking at all of the different components of that economy and figuring out how they might affect each other. World 2030 is a study that sets up nine groups (AI labs, big employers, banks and insurers, utilities, startups, universities, workers, governments, and the Fed) and runs the US economy forward in six-month turns to 2030. It aimed to identify both the invariants and the boundaries of what can change as these powerful forces interact with each other. The study predicts that AI will break per-seat software pricing and cut US junior desk hiring.

entry.title: Unlocking Stable On-Policy RL on TPU with Bitwise-Zero Train–Inference Mismatch (7 minute read)
entry.content:
Google's ZERO-TIM implementation, verified across 64 TPU v5p chips, achieves bitwise-identical logprobs for sampler and trainer, ensuring true on-policy stability in RL training by eliminating numerical discrepancies. This solution addresses floating-point addition errors in separate serving and training paths, using consistent arithmetic operations and standardized reduction orders across TPU meshes.

entry.title: On the Brutality of Amdahl's Law (12 minute read)
entry.content:
The world is far too slow to see the high double-digit or more economic growth and seismic transformations in the economy that AI is predicted to bring. Intelligence isn't the only technology curve to go quasi-infinite in the last century and a half. Electricity, communication, computers, transportation, and agriculture have all experienced extreme growth and transformation. Despite this, we've only seen 2% GDP per capita growth for nearly 150 years.

entry.title: Eliminating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference with Integer-Only Arithmetic (15 minute read)
entry.content:
A floating-point number stores a fixed number of significant digits and a separate exponent. When two numbers with very different exponents are added, the small one has to be shifted to line up with the big one, and the digits that fall off on the end are gone. That means that (a+b)+c is not always equal to a+(b+c). This post looks at what happens when integer addition, which is exact, is used.

entry.title: How Agent Anomaly Detection scores on benchmarks we didn't write (8 minute read)
entry.content:

It demonstrated varying false alarm rates, with the highest at 16% for tasks involving high-impact tools. Ongoing improvements focus on detecting small, potentially harmful actions, distinguishing normal use from misuse, and providing quicker full coverage for new agents.

entry.title: MCP vs CLI vs Skills: What Each Costs in Context (11 minute read)
entry.content:
MCP servers significantly increase token use, adding thousands of input tokens per request, unlike CLI or skill methods. On Sonnet 5.5, a simple task showed MCP consuming 59,417 tokens with default tools against CLI's 1,421 and skill's 3,315, highlighting the high cost of tool-heavy MCP setups. Implementing Tool Search can cut token costs by deferring tool definitions, reducing upfront toolset costs to under 600 tokens for optimal efficiency.

From TLDR AI · 2026-11-12 · Deep Dives & Analysis

entry.title: LLMs can learn some multi-step reasoning on filler tokens instead of visible CoT (9 minute read)
entry.content:
By changing the training setup and applying LoRAs to Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and gpt-oss-20b, researchers taught models to do some multi-step tasks while emitting only filler tokens, beating an answer-only baseline on three of seven tasks. They also mapped theoretical layer-depth limits and showed empirical walls, with some tasks learned out to 60 steps and others failing after one to three. The work is meant to separate filler-token reasoning from steganographic hidden reasoning when interpreting chain-of-thought.

entry.title: What objective is reasoning solving? (12 minute read)
entry.content:
Reasoning is pathfinding in token space. There are many paths from the problem to a correct answer, and the model traverses each of them with each sample. A path is not guaranteed to converge to the correct answer - it's only in aggregate, over the distribution of paths, do we get a high probability of success. RL training directly raises the success probability. The gains credited to 'thinking longer' come from the search paid for during training rather than at inference.

From TLDR AI · 2026-11-10 · Engineering & Research

entry.title: Two Kinds of Test-Time Scaling (28 minute read)
entry.content:
Test-time scaling trades compute for performance at test time. There are two types of test-time scaling: one allows researchers to trade more compute for more performance per task, but only up to the maximum quantity of per-task compute used during training; and the other lets researchers trade more compute for more performance per task, and lets them do so up to quantities of compute and performance that never occurred during training. Scaling methods that permit the latter change will have a larger impact than test-time scaling considered simply. This essay describes how this may impact the world.
